title: A t-exact triangulated functor preserves the cohomology boundary comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure], hearts $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, and heart-valued cohomology functors $H^r_{\mathcal C},H^r_{\mathcal D}$ [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an exact functor equipped with coherent shift comparisons $\sigma_{M,r}:P(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(PM)[r]$. Suppose that $P$ preserves both halves of the t-structures, in every integer degree. Write $P^{\heartsuit}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ for its restriction. The canonical truncation comparisons [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison], together with $\sigma$, give natural isomorphisms
$$c^r_M:P^{\heartsuit}H^r_{\mathcal C}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r_{\mathcal D}(PM).$$
For a distinguished triangle $T=(A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{w}A[1])$, let $PT$ have last arrow $\sigma_{A,1}\circ P(w)$, and let $\delta_T^r:H^r_{\mathcal C}(C)\to H^{r+1}_{\mathcal C}(A)$ and $\delta_{PT}^r:H^r_{\mathcal D}(PC)\to H^{r+1}_{\mathcal D}(PA)$ be its standard cohomology boundaries. Then, for every integer $r$,
$$c^{r+1}_A\circ P^{\heartsuit}(\delta_T^r)=\delta_{PT}^r\circ c^r_C.$$
These comparison squares are natural in morphisms of distinguished triangles.

source.place: BBD Proposition 1.3.3 (canonical truncation adjunctions), Theorem 1.3.6 (heart and cohomological functor), and 1.3.16 (t-exact functors), printed pp. 29–31 and 36–37; boundary compatibility is the generic formal comparison extracted by the agent from these constructions, not printed as a separate theorem. No Stacks tag states this t-structure form.

proof.text:
Since $P$ preserves both halves, it sends the full heart $\mathcal A=\mathcal C^{\le0}\cap\mathcal C^{\ge0}$ into $\mathcal B$; its restriction $P^{\heartsuit}$ is therefore defined. Write $Q_{\mathcal C}=H^0_{\mathcal C}=\tau^{\ge0}_{\mathcal C}\tau^{\le0}_{\mathcal C}$ and similarly $Q_{\mathcal D}$. Apply [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] at $m=0$ to $P$ (the categories have bounded t-structures and $P$ is exact and preserves both halves in every degree, exactly its hypotheses). If $\alpha^-,\alpha^+$ are its natural isomorphisms, their composite
$$e_M=\tau^{\ge0}_{\mathcal D}(\alpha^-_{P,0,M})\circ\alpha^+_{P,0,\tau^{\le0}_{\mathcal C}M}:P^{\heartsuit}Q_{\mathcal C}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal D}(PM)$$
is an isomorphism in the full heart. This uses the stated formula for $H^0$ in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1); fullness means that the displayed ambient morphism and its inverse are also heart morphisms.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), Theorem 1.3.6, and 1.3.16; printed pp. 29–31, 36: composite of the two canonical truncation comparisons

proof.text:
The composite $e$ is natural: for any $f:M\to N$, naturality of $\alpha^+$ followed by naturality of $\alpha^-$, with $\tau^{\ge0}_{\mathcal D}$ applied to the latter equation, gives
$$e_N\circ P^{\heartsuit}(Q_{\mathcal C}(f))=Q_{\mathcal D}(P(f))\circ e_M.$$
No boundary assertion is taken from [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison]; only its naturality in the object is used here.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i): naturality of the two adjunction comparisons, composed

proof.text:
Use the convention $H^r(M)=Q(M[r])$ of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1). The comparison in degree $r$ is explicitly
$$c^r_M=Q_{\mathcal D}(\sigma_{M,r})\circ e_{M[r]}.$$
It is an isomorphism since each factor is. This is precisely the canonical truncation comparison together with the given shift comparison: $e$ is the composite of the canonical truncation maps at zero, now evaluated on $M[r]$. For $f:M\to N$, apply step 2 to $f[r]$ and then use $\sigma_{N,r}P(f[r])=(P(f))[r]\sigma_{M,r}$ to obtain
$$c^r_N P^{\heartsuit}(H^r_{\mathcal C}(f))=H^r_{\mathcal D}(P(f))c^r_M.$$
Thus all $c^r$ are natural, for positive, zero and negative $r$.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.6 and 1.3.16; printed pp. 31, 36: shifted cohomology and naturality of the supplied shift comparison

proof.text:
Fix $r$ and let $a_{X,r}:(X[1])[r]\xrightarrow{\sim}X[r+1]$ be the associator for the iterated shift. Put $w_r=a_{A,r}\circ w[r]$ and $v=\sigma_{A,1}\circ P(w)$, so the shifted third arrow of $PT$ is $v_r=a_{PA,r}\circ v[r]$. Coherence of the given $\sigma$ says
$$\sigma_{A,r+1}\circ P(a_{A,r})=a_{PA,r}\circ(\sigma_{A,1})[r]\circ\sigma_{A[1],r}.$$
Naturality of $\sigma_{-,r}$ at $w:C\to A[1]$ says $\sigma_{A[1],r}P(w[r])=(P(w))[r]\sigma_{C,r}$. Substitute this into the preceding equation and use functoriality of $[r]$ to get
$$\sigma_{A,r+1}\circ P(w_r)=v_r\circ\sigma_{C,r}.$$
This is a calculation from the specified coherent shift data, not an additional theorem about t-exact functors. Exactness of $P$ in [def-weil-triangulated-category] ensures that the image triangle with third arrow $v$ is distinguished.

source.place: 1.1.1, printed p. 18; 1.3.16, printed p. 36: shifts and the exact-functor structure; explicit coherence calculation

proof.text:
By the definition of the standard long exact sequence of the cohomological functor in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](5), its boundary is $\delta_T^r=Q_{\mathcal C}(w_r)$; likewise $\delta_{PT}^r=Q_{\mathcal D}(v_r)$. There is no extra rotation sign here: these are the shifted third arrows, followed by the shift associator. Apply step 2 to $w_r:C[r]\to A[r+1]$, substitute step 4, and preserve composition under $Q_{\mathcal D}$. The whole required square is the following calculation:
$$\begin{aligned}
c^{r+1}_A P^{\heartsuit}(\delta_T^r)
&=Q_{\mathcal D}(\sigma_{A,r+1})e_{A[r+1]}P^{\heartsuit}(Q_{\mathcal C}(w_r))\\
&=Q_{\mathcal D}(\sigma_{A,r+1}\circ P(w_r))e_{C[r]}\\
&=Q_{\mathcal D}(v_r\circ\sigma_{C,r})e_{C[r]}\\
&=\delta_{PT}^r c^r_C.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the boundary compatibility is proved using object naturality of $e$, rather than assumed as a property of the truncation comparisons.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.6, printed p. 31: boundary of a cohomological functor; explicit naturality calculation (cf. Mathlib HomologicalFunctor.lean, definition homologySequenceδ, lines 172–178)

proof.text: For a morphism of triangles $(a,b,d):T\to T'$, its third-arrow equation is $a[1]\circ w=w'\circ d$ by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Shift it by $r$ and use naturality of the associator to obtain $a[r+1]\circ w_r=w'_r\circ d[r]$. Applying $Q_{\mathcal C}$ gives $H^{r+1}_{\mathcal C}(a)\delta_T^r=\delta_{T'}^rH^r_{\mathcal C}(d)$. The same calculation applies in $\mathcal D$ to $PT\to PT'$: its third-arrow equation follows by applying $P$ and using naturality of $\sigma_{-,1}$. Finally step 3 gives the commuting comparison faces at $a$ and $d$. Together with step 5 these are all the faces expressing naturality of the comparison square in a morphism of distinguished triangles.
